1:10.headline: Pharaoh says 'they will leave', the sages hear 'we will leave'
1:10.body: Plainly, Pharaoh fears Israel will go up out of the land. The sages read it as 'we will go up from the land': Pharaoh meant his own people, and the verse hangs the bad words on someone else.

sources.quote: כְּאָדָם שֶׁמְּקַלֵּל עַצְמוֹ וְתוֹלֶה קִלְלָתוֹ בַּאֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi brings the sages' reading: like a man who curses himself but hangs the curse on others, as if it said 'we will go up from the land'.

sources.quote: כנה הכתוב כי היה לו לומר ועלינו
sources.says: Bahya says the verse used a softer word, since it should have said 'and we will go up'.

sources.quote: כי טעם ועלה מן הארץ, כמו ועלינו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Marinus with the 'we will go up' reading, but says he sees no need for it.

1:12.headline: The Egyptians were sick of Israel, who were like thorns to them
1:12.body: ויקצו means they loathed or dreaded the Israelites. The sages hear קוצים, 'thorns', in it: the Israelites were like thorns in the Egyptians' eyes.

sources.quote: קָצוּ בְחַיֵּיהֶם. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָרְשׁוּ כְּקוֹצִים הָיוּ בְּעֵינֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they were sick of their lives, and the sages read it as 'they were like thorns in their eyes'.

sources.quote: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ דּוֹמִין בְּעֵינֵיהֶם כְּקוֹצִים
sources.says: The Talmud says this teaches that the Israelites looked like thorns to them.

sources.quote: בחייהם, כמו: קצתי בחיי
sources.says: Rashbam reads it as being sick of their lives, as in 'I am weary of my life'.

1:15.headline: Puah: the midwife who cooed to the babies
1:15.body: The sages say Puah was Miriam. Her name means calling out: she cooed to soothe the newborn, or, says the Talmud, she cried out a prophecy that her mother would bear Israel's savior.

sources.quote: זוֹ מִרְיָם, שֶׁפּוֹעָה וּמְדַבֶּרֶת וְהוֹגָה לַוָּלָד
sources.says: Rashi says Puah is Miriam, who cooed and spoke softly to the newborn.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צְעָקָה, כְּמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says פועה is a word for crying out, as in 'like a woman in labor I will cry out'.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיְתָה פּוֹעָה בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ וְאוֹמֶרֶת: עֲתִידָה אִמִּי שֶׁתֵּלֵד בֵּן שֶׁמּוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: The Talmud says she cried out with the holy spirit that her mother would bear a son who would save Israel.

10:1.headline: Why God tells Moses now: 'I hardened his heart'
10:1.body: Rashbam notes that through the earlier plagues God did not tell Moses that He was hardening Pharaoh's heart. He says it here because Pharaoh had just admitted 'the Lord is righteous' and still refused. Ramban adds that the Egyptians had been frightened by the hail and had confessed.

sources.quote: בכל מכות לא מצינו שהודיע הקב"ה למשה שחיזק את לבו. אך בזאת שהודה פרעה שהוא הצדיק ואני ועמי הרשעים
sources.says: Rashbam says that in no other plague did God tell Moses He had hardened Pharaoh's heart, but here Pharaoh had admitted 'the Lord is righteous and I and my people are wicked'.

sources.quote: שֶׁהוּא הִכְבִּיד אֶת לִבָּם עַתָּה אַחֲרֵי שֶׁפָּחֲדוּ מִמֶּנּוּ בַּבָּרָד וְהִתְוַדּוּ עַל עֲוֹנָם
sources.says: Ramban says God hardened their hearts now, after they had feared Him during the hail and confessed their sin.

10:2.headline: What God 'did' in Egypt: deeds, or mockery
10:2.body: Rashi says התעללתי means 'I made sport of them', as Balaam says to his donkey 'you have mocked me'. A word for plain deeds would be עוללתי. Rashbam reads it as deeds. Rabbeinu Bahya brings a midrash: as they stripped my vineyard (עוללו), so I strip them from the world.

sources.quote: שָׂחַקְתִּי, כְּמוֹ "כִּי הִתְעַלַּלְתְּ בִּי"
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'I made sport', as in 'for you have mocked me'.

sources.quote: וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן פּוֹעֵל וּמַעֲלָלִים, שֶׁאִם כֵּן הָיָה לוֹ לִכְתֹּב עוֹלַלְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi says it is not a word for deeds, because then it would have been written עוללתי.

sources.quote: התעללתי - פעולת עלילות
sources.says: Rashbam says it means doing deeds.

sources.quote: כשם שהם עוללו את כרמי כך אני מעולל אותם מן העולם
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites a midrash: as they stripped My vineyard, so I strip them from the world.

10:2.headline: 'Tell your son': a hint that locusts were coming
10:2.body: The verse does not say what the next plague is. The Tur HaArokh cites a midrash that 'tell your son and your son's son' was the hint, since the prophet Joel says of locusts 'tell your children of it'. Bekhor Shor adds that locusts are something people tell stories about more than other plagues.

sources.quote: דורש שהודיעו ברמז מדכתיב למען תספר באזני בנך ובן בנך זאת מכת הארבה כמה דתימא עלי' לבניכם ספרו
sources.says: The Tur HaArokh cites a midrash that 'so you may tell your son' hinted at the locusts, as Joel says 'tell your children of it'.

sources.quote: בארבה שייך ספור דברים יותר משאר מכות
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says locusts are more a thing people tell about than the other plagues.

10:10.headline: 'Evil is before you', or a star named Ra'ah
10:10.body: Onkelos reads Pharaoh's words as a threat: the evil you plan will turn back on your own faces. Rashi brings a midrash: Pharaoh saw by his astrology a star called רעה rising over them in the desert, a sign of blood. Moses later pleads that Egypt not say God brought them out 'with ra'ah'.

sources.quote: באור הכתוב כתרגומו בישא דאתון סבירין למעבד לקבל אפיכון לאסתחרא
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya explains the verse as Onkelos does: the evil you mean to do will turn back against your faces.

sources.quote: כּוֹכָב אֶחָד יֵשׁ שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ רָעָה, אָמַר לָהֶם פַּרְעֹה, רוֹאֶה אֲנִי בָּאִצְטַגְנִינוּת שֶׁלִּי אוֹתוֹ כוֹכָב עוֹלֶה לִקְרַאתְכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר, וְהוּא סִימַן דָּם וַהֲרִיגָה
sources.says: Rashi cites a midrash: a star named Ra'ah, which Pharaoh saw by astrology rising toward them in the desert, a sign of blood and killing.

sources.quote: לָמָּה יֹאמְרוּ מִצְרַיִם לֵאמֹר "בְּרָעָה" הוֹצִיאָם
sources.says: Rashi links it to Moses' later prayer: why should Egypt say He brought them out 'with ra'ah'?

10:13.headline: The east wind is the 'front' wind, where the sun starts
10:13.body: Ibn Ezra and Chizkuni say the east is called קדים, from קדם, front or first, because the sun rises there first. That is why the west is called אחור, behind.

sources.quote: ונקרא קדים בעבור שהוא נקדם בפאות כי משם תחל השמש לזרוח, על כן נקרא מערב אחור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is called קדים because it is first among the directions, where the sun begins to rise, and so the west is called 'behind'.

sources.quote: רוח קדים הוא רוח מזרח ונקרא כן שממנו תקדים השמש לזרוח
sources.says: Chizkuni says the east wind is called קדים because from there the sun rises first.

10:17.headline: Why Pharaoh calls the locusts 'this death'
10:17.body: Rabbeinu Bahya gives two readings. Perhaps people really died in the locust plague, as they did in the hail. Or, after the hail and the locusts, no food was left, and that was death for them.

sources.quote: למדך שהיו בני אדם מתים במכת הארבה כשם שהיו מתים במכת הברד
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says this teaches that people died in the locust plague as they died in the hail.

sources.quote: ואחר שתי מכות אלה לא נשתיירה מחיה לבני אדם בארץ, והנה זה להם מות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya also says that after these two plagues no food was left in the land, which was death for them.

10:19.headline: Not one locust left, not even the salted ones
10:19.body: Rashi says 'not one' is exact: even the locusts the Egyptians had salted to eat were swept away. Rabbeinu Bahya says Moses' prayer still holds, so that locusts do no damage in Egypt.

sources.quote: לא נשאר ארבה אחד. אַף הַמְּלוּחִים שֶׁמָּלְחוּ מֵהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says not one locust remained, not even the ones they had salted.

sources.quote: תפלתו של משה במכת הארבה היא שעמדה עד היום שאין ארבה מפסיד בכל גבול מצרים
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says Moses' prayer in the locust plague stands to this day, so locusts do no harm anywhere in Egypt.

10:23.headline: Light 'where they lived': wherever an Israelite was
10:23.body: In other plagues the verse names the land of Goshen. Here it says only 'in their dwellings'. Chizkuni and Rashbam say this means light went with each Israelite, even into an Egyptian's house.

sources.quote: היה אור במושבתם בארץ גשן אין כתיב כאן כמו במכות אחרות
sources.says: Chizkuni notes the verse does not say 'in the land of Goshen' as with other plagues.

sources.quote: שאפילו כשהיה ישראל בבית המצרי במצרים היה אור עמו
sources.says: Chizkuni says even when an Israelite was in an Egyptian's house, the light was with him.

sources.quote: אפילו שהוא יושב אצל בית המצרי
sources.says: Rashbam says the light was there even when he stayed by an Egyptian's house.

10:29.headline: 'You have spoken well': Moses agrees, but not as Pharaoh meant
10:29.body: Pharaoh says Moses will die if he sees his face again. Rashi has Moses answer: you spoke well and at the right time, I will not see your face again. Chizkuni adds the sting: but you will need to see mine.

sources.quote: יָפֶה דִּבַּרְתָּ וּבִזְמַנּוֹ דִּבַּרְתָּ. אֱמֶת שֶׁלֹּא אוֹסִיף עוֹד רְאוֹת פָּנֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says Moses meant: you spoke well and at the right time; it is true I will not see your face again.

sources.quote: לא אסף עוד ראות פניך אבל אתה תצטרך לראות פני
sources.says: Chizkuni says Moses meant: I will not see your face again, but you will need to see mine.

11:2.headline: Borrow, or ask for a gift?
11:2.body: שאל can mean to borrow or simply to ask. Rashbam says Israel asked for outright gifts, while Chizkuni says they borrowed, so that the Egyptians would be eager to chase after them.

sources.quote: וישאלו - לשם מתנה גמורה כמו: שאל ממני ואתנה גוים נחלתך
sources.says: Rashbam says they asked for a full gift, as in "ask of me and I will give nations as your inheritance".

sources.quote: בענין שאלה ולא בענין מתנה כדי שיהיו מצריים להוטים לרדוף אחריהם
sources.says: Chizkuni says it was a loan and not a gift, so that the Egyptians would be eager to pursue them.

11:2.headline: Egyptians called "friends": the plagues had changed them
11:2.body: Each Israelite asks "from his friend", meaning an Egyptian neighbor. Chizkuni asks how Egyptians could be called friends, and answers that after the plagues they had come to like Israel.

sources.quote: וכי מצרים היו להם רעים לישראל אלא מלמד שאחרי המכות היו כרעים ואוהבים ישראל
sources.says: Chizkuni asks whether Egyptians were friends of Israel, and says that after the plagues they were like friends who loved Israel.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ אַנְשֵׁי מִצְרַיִם שׂוֹנְאִים אוֹתָם עַל הַמַּכּוֹת, אֲבָל מוֹסִיפִין בָּהֶם אַהֲבָה
sources.says: Ramban says the Egyptians did not hate Israel for the plagues, but grew fonder of them.

11:4.headline: "I will go out": how does God go out into Egypt?
11:4.body: Onkelos translates "I will be revealed", and HaKtav VeHaKabalah says he did so to avoid picturing God as a body that moves. Ibn Ezra says it is God's decree that goes out, while Chizkuni says God goes himself because Pharaoh would not listen to his messengers.

sources.quote: אֲנָא מִתְגְלִי בְּגוֹ מִצְרָיִם
sources.says: Onkelos translates "I will be revealed in the midst of Egypt".

sources.quote: ת"א אנא מתגלי, הרחיק את ההגשמה
sources.says: HaKtav VeHaKabalah says Onkelos translated "I will be revealed" to keep away from picturing God as a body.

sources.quote: וטעם אני יוצא, על הגזרה היוצאת מאת השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says "I go out" refers to the decree that goes out from God.

sources.quote: הואיל ואינו שומע בקול שלוחי ארד אני בכבודי
sources.says: Chizkuni says that since Pharaoh does not listen to God's messengers, God will come down himself.

11:5.headline: "Who sits on his throne": the heir, not Pharaoh himself
11:5.body: Pharaoh sat on the throne, not his son. Onkelos, Ibn Ezra and Ralbag read the phrase as the firstborn who was due to sit on the throne after him.

sources.quote: מִבּוּכְרָא דְפַרְעֹה דְעָתִיד לְמִתַּב עַל כָּרְסֵי מַלְכוּתֵהּ
sources.says: Onkelos translates "from Pharaoh's firstborn, who is destined to sit on his royal throne".

sources.quote: היושב על כסאו. הראוי לשבת על כסאו אחריו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the one fit to sit on his throne after him.

sources.ref: Ralbag Beur HaMilot on Torah, Exodus 11:5:1
sources.quote: הראוי להיות יושב על כסאו כי בנו הבכור היה ראוי שימלוך תחתיו אחריו
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the one fit to sit on the throne, since the eldest son was due to reign after him.

11:8.headline: "Your servants will come down": Moses spares the king's pride
11:8.body: In the end Pharaoh himself came to Moses at night. Rashi and Rashbam say Moses named only the servants out of respect for the king.

sources.quote: חָלַק כָּבוֹד לַמַּלְכוּת, שֶׁהֲרֵי בַּסּוֹף יָרַד פַּרְעֹה בְּעַצְמוֹ אֵלָיו בַּלַּיְלָה
sources.says: Rashi says Moses showed respect to the king, since in the end Pharaoh himself came down to him at night.

sources.quote: וירדו כל עבדיך - דרך כבוד אמר לו
sources.says: Rashbam says Moses spoke this way out of respect.

12:2.headline: This month: God points at the new moon
12:2.body: Rashi stops on the word הזה, this one. Moses was unsure how big the new moon must be before it counts, so God pointed at the moon in the sky and said: see one like this, and declare the month.

sources.quote: נִתְקַשָּׁה מֹשֶׁה עַל מוֹלַד הַלְּבָנָה, בְּאֵיזוֹ שִׁעוּר תֵּרָאֶה וְתִהְיֶה רְאוּיָה לְקַדֵּשׁ, וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ בְּאֶצְבַּע אֶת הַלְּבָנָה בָּרָקִיעַ וְאָמַר לוֹ כָּזֶה רְאֵה וְקַדֵּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says Moses found the new moon hard to judge, so God showed him the moon with a finger and said: see one like this and sanctify it.

12:6.headline: Between the two evenings: which two?
12:6.body: The phrase is literally between the evenings. Rashi says the first evening starts after noon, when shadows lengthen, and the second at nightfall. Ibn Ezra calls it a hard word and says the two are sunset and the fading of the sun's light, about an hour and a third apart.

sources.quote: מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה קָרוּי בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם, שֶׁהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ נוֹטֶה לְבֵית מְבוֹאוֹ לַעֲרֹב
sources.says: Rashi says from the sixth hour on is called between the evenings, since the sun turns toward its setting.

sources.quote: בין הערבים. מלה קשה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says between the evenings is a hard phrase.

sources.quote: והנה יש לנו שני ערבים האחד עריבת השמש, והוא עת ביאתו תחת הארץ, והשני ביאת אורו הנראה בעבים והנה יש ביניהם קרוב משעה ושליש שעה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the two evenings are sunset and the end of its light seen in the clouds, about an hour and a third apart.

12:9.headline: A word for half-cooked meat found nowhere else
12:9.body: נא appears only here in this sense. Rashi says it is meat not roasted enough, and that this is its name in Arabic. Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner in the Bible and means raw, as in Arabic.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָלוּי כָּל צָרְכּוֹ קוֹרְאוֹ נָא בְלָשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי
sources.says: Rashi says meat that is not fully roasted is called נא in Arabic.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שאין לו חבר במקרא, ופירושו הפך מבושל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner in Scripture and means the opposite of cooked.

sources.quote: והבשר החי יקראו בלשון ערבי ניי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says raw meat is called ניי in Arabic.

12:11.headline: Passover is named for God skipping over the houses
12:11.body: Rashi says the offering is called פסח for skipping: God jumped from Egyptian house to Egyptian house and passed over the Israelite one in between. He adds that Israel should do the service in a skipping, hurried way to recall the name.

sources.quote: הַקָּרְבָּן קָרוּי פסח עַל שֵׁם הַדִּלּוּג וְהַפְּסִיחָה
sources.says: Rashi says the offering is called פסח because of the skipping and passing over.

sources.quote: וְאַתֶּם עֲשׂוּ כָל עֲבוֹדוֹתָיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, דֶּרֶךְ דִּלּוּג וּקְפִיצָה, זֵכֶר לִשְׁמוֹ שֶׁקָּרוּי פסח
sources.says: Rashi says Israel should do all its service in a skipping, leaping way, to recall its name.

sources.quote: שהמלאך ידלג ויניח בית ישראל להכות בכורות שבבתי מצרים
sources.says: Rashbam says the angel would skip and leave the Israelite house, to strike the firstborn in Egyptian houses.

12:13.headline: I will pass over you, or I will have pity on you
12:13.body: Onkelos translates ופסחתי as I will have pity, and Rashi gives that reading first. Then Rashi says his own view: every פסיחה means skipping and jumping, as God skipped over Israelite houses mixed in among Egyptian ones.

sources.quote: ופסחתי. וְחָמַלְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi first explains it as: I will have pity.

sources.quote: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, כָּל פְּסִיחָה לְשׁוֹן דִּלּוּג וּקְפִיצָה
sources.says: Rashi says that in his view every use of the word means skipping and jumping.

sources.quote: וְאֶחֱזֵי יָת דְמָא וְאֵיחוֹס עֲלֵיכוֹן
sources.says: Onkelos translates: I will see the blood and have pity on you.

12:15.headline: The first day here means the day before the festival
12:15.body: It sounds like the first of the seven days. Rashi says it means the day before them, since ראשון can mean earlier. So the leaven must be gone on the eve of Passover.

sources.quote: מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב, וְקָרוּי רִאשׁוֹן לְפִי שֶׁהוּא לִפְנֵי הַשִּׁבְעָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the eve of the festival, called first because it comes before the seven days.

sources.quote: וּמָצִינוּ מֻקְדָּם קָרוּי רִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says we find that what came earlier is called ראשון.

12:17.headline: Guard the matzot, and guard the mitzvot
12:17.body: מצות, matzot, has the same letters as מצוות, commandments. Rabbi Yoshiah reads it both ways: just as you do not let matzah sit and rise, do not let a commandment wait. Do it as soon as it comes to you.

sources.quote: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אוֹמֵר אַל תְּהִי קוֹרֵא אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת, אֶלָּא אֶת הַמִּצְווֹת – כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאֵין מַחֲמִיצִין אֶת הַמַּצָּה, כָּךְ אֵין מַחֲמִיצִין אֶת הַמִּצְוָה
sources.says: Rashi quotes Rabbi Yoshiah: read it as commandments, for just as one does not let matzah rise, one does not let a commandment go stale.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא אִם בָּאָה לְיָדְךָ, עֲשֵׂה אוֹתָהּ מִיָּד
sources.says: Rashi says if a commandment comes your way, do it right away.

12:21.headline: Draw out a lamb, or draw your hands away from idols
12:21.body: משכו means draw. Rashi reads it simply: whoever has sheep should draw one from his own flock. In the Mekhilta, Rabbi Yose the Galilean reads it as: draw your hands away from idol worship and hold on to the commandment.

sources.quote: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ צֹאן יִמְשֹׁךְ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says whoever has sheep should draw one from his own.

sources.quote: רַבִּי יוֹסֵה הַגָּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: מִשְׁכוּ יְדֵיכֶם מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְהִדָּבְקוּ בַּמִּצְוָה
sources.says: Rabbi Yose the Galilean says: draw your hands away from idol worship and cling to the commandment.

12:29.headline: And the LORD: God together with His heavenly court
12:29.body: The verse says ויהוה, and the LORD, with an extra ו. Rashi says that wherever God's name has this ו, it means God and His court, because the ו adds someone, like saying this one and that one.

sources.quote: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַה'" הוּא וּבֵית דִּינוֹ, שֶׁהַוָּי"ו לְשׁוֹן תּוֹסֶפֶת הוּא, כְּמוֹ פְּלוֹנִי וּפְלוֹנִי
sources.says: Rashi says wherever it says and the LORD, it means He and His court, since the ו adds, as in so-and-so and so-and-so.

12:34.headline: Kneading bowls, or the leftovers of the seder
12:34.body: Rashbam and Ibn Ezra say משארתם are kneading bowls, as in the blessing on your basket and your kneading bowl. Rashi reads it from שאר, what remains: the leftover matzah and bitter herbs, which they carried on their shoulders.

sources.quote: משארתם. שְׁיָרֵי מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says it means the leftovers of matzah and bitter herbs.

sources.quote: הוא הכלי שנותנין בו הבצק וזה מוכיח ברוך טנאך ומשארתך
sources.says: Rashbam says it is the vessel the dough is put in, as the blessing on your basket and kneading bowl shows.

sources.quote: כלי עץ כמו טנאך ומשארתך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a wooden vessel, as in your basket and your kneading bowl.

12:36.headline: They emptied Egypt like a net with no grain
12:36.body: Onkelos and Rashi translate וינצלו as they emptied. The Talmud hears two sound-alike words in it: Egypt was left like a trap with no grain in it, or like the deep sea with no fish.

sources.quote: וינצלו. וְרוֹקִינוּ
sources.says: Rashi gives the Aramaic: and they emptied.

sources.quote: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּדָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגָן, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר, עֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים
sources.says: Rabbi Ami says they made Egypt like a trap with no grain, and Resh Lakish says like the deep with no fish.

12:42.headline: A night of watching: God waited for it, and God guards it
12:42.body: Rashi gives both senses of שמרים. God was watching and waiting for this night to keep His promise, and the night is guarded, so harmful forces cannot strike. Rashbam reads it as waiting, as in his father kept the matter in mind.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה הַקָּבָּ"ה שׁוֹמֵר וּמְצַפֶּה לוֹ, לְקַיֵּם הַבְטָחָתוֹ להוציאם מארץ מצרים
sources.says: Rashi says God was watching and waiting for it, to keep His promise to bring them out of Egypt.

sources.quote: מְשֻׁמָּר וּבָא מִן הַמַּזִּיקִין
sources.says: Rashi says the night is guarded from harmful forces.

sources.quote: לשון המתנה כמו: ואביו שמר את הדבר
sources.says: Rashbam says the word means waiting, as in his father kept the matter in mind.

12:43.headline: A stranger, or a Jew who has become a stranger
12:43.body: בן נכר usually means a foreigner. Rashi says it means anyone whose deeds became foreign to his Father in heaven. So it covers a non-Jew and also a Jew who left the faith.

sources.quote: שֶׁנִּתְנַכְּרוּ מַעֲשָׂיו לְאָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, וְאֶחָד הַגּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשֻׁמָּד בְּמַשְׁמָע
sources.says: Rashi says it means one whose deeds became estranged from his Father in heaven, both a non-Jew and a Jew who left the faith.

13:8.headline: 'Because of this': did God act so we would keep mitzvot?
13:8.body: Rashi reads 'because of this' as: God took me out so that I would keep these mitzvot, the Passover offering, matza and bitter herbs. Ramban reads it the other way: because of what God did for me, I do this service.

sources.quote: בַּעֲבוּר שֶׁאֲקַיֵּם מִצְווֹתָיו, כְּגוֹן פֶּסַח מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר הַלָּלוּ
sources.says: Rashi says 'this' means so that I will keep his mitzvot, such as the Passover offering, matza and bitter herbs.

sources.quote: כִּי בַּעֲבוּר זֶה שֶׁעָשָׂה ה' לִי בְּצֵאתִי מִמִּצְרָיִם אֲנִי עוֹבֵד אֶת הָעֲבוֹדָה הַזֹּאת
sources.says: Ramban says the meaning is: because of what God did for me when I left Egypt, I do this service.

13:9.headline: A sign on your hand: real object or figure of speech?
13:9.body: Rashbam says the deep plain sense is 'remember it always, as if it were written on your hand'. Ibn Ezra rejects reading it as a figure of speech. He says it means what it says, as the sages taught.

sources.quote: לפי עומק פשוטו: יהיה לך לזכרון תמיד, כאלו כתוב על ידך
sources.says: Rashbam says by its deep plain sense the verse means: remember it always, as if it were written on your hand.

sources.quote: רק הוא כמשמעו, על כן לא נוציאנו מיד פשוטו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the verse means just what it says, and we will not take it away from its plain meaning.

14:10.headline: A whole army chasing them, in the singular
14:10.body: Egypt is a whole army, but the verb נסע is singular. Rashi says they chased with one heart, like one man. Or Israel saw Egypt's heavenly prince coming to help.

sources.quote: נסע אחריהם. בְּלֵב אֶחָד כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says they chased with one heart, like one man.

sources.quote: רָאוּ שַׂר שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם נוֹסֵעַ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם לַעֲזֹר לַמִּצְרִים
sources.says: Rashi's second reading: they saw Egypt's heavenly prince setting out to help the Egyptians.

14:25.headline: Pharaoh made his heart heavy, so God made the chariots heavy
14:25.body: Rashi says God drove the chariots 'heavily' (בכבדת) to repay Pharaoh in kind. Pharaoh had made his own heart heavy (ויכבד) against letting the people go.

sources.quote: בַּמִדָּה שֶׁמָּדְדוּ: "וַיַּכְבֵּד" לִבּוֹ הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו (שמות ט'), אַף כָּאן וַיְנַהֲגֵהוּ "בִּכְבֵדֻת"
sources.says: Rashi says it was measure for measure: he made his heart heavy, so here God drove them heavily.

15:1.headline: 'Then Moses will sing': why the future tense?
15:1.body: Rashi says it means the thought to sing rose in Moses' heart when he saw the miracle, and then he sang. The sages read the future tense as a hint, in the Torah itself, that the dead will rise.

sources.quote: אז כשראה הנס עלה בלבו שישיר שירה
sources.says: Rashi says when Moses saw the miracle, it rose in his heart to sing a song.

sources.quote: מכאן רמז לתחית המתים מן התורה
sources.says: Rashi quotes the sages: from here is a hint of the resurrection of the dead in the Torah.

15:1.headline: 'Highly exalted': above the proud, beyond all praise, or victorious?
15:1.body: Onkelos reads גאה גאה as 'He rose above the proud'. Rashi adds that however much one praises Him there is more, while Rashbam says גאות here means victory in war.

sources.quote: ארי אתגאי על גותניא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: for He is exalted over the proud.

sources.quote: על כל השירות וכל מה שאקלס בו, עוד יש בו תוספת
sources.says: Rashi says beyond every song and praise I give Him, there is still more.

sources.quote: נצחון מלחמה קורין גאות
sources.says: Rashbam says victory in war is called גאות.

15:1.headline: Thrown up high, then down to the depths
15:1.body: Here the horses are thrown with רמה, which sounds like רום, height, and in verse 4 with ירה. A midrash in Rashi says both happened: they were tossed up high and then down to the depths.

sources.quote: כתוב אחד אומר רמה, וכתוב אחד אומר ירה, מלמד שהיו עולין לרום ויורדין לתהום
sources.says: Rashi quotes a midrash: one verse says רמה and another ירה, teaching that they rose up high and went down to the deep.

15:2.headline: God as my song, or God cutting down the enemy?
15:2.body: Onkelos reads זמרת as song, 'my praise'. Rashi reads it from זמר, to prune or cut: God's might and His cutting down of the enemy became our rescue.

sources.quote: תקפי ותשבחתי
sources.says: Onkelos translates: my strength and my praise.

sources.quote: ולשון וזמרת לשון "לא תזמר" (ויקרא כ"ה), "זמיר עריצים" (ישעיהו כ"ה), לשון כסוח וכריתה
sources.says: Rashi says וזמרת is like 'do not prune', a word for cutting down.

sources.quote: וזמרת לאויבי שזומר ומחתך אותם
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says it is a cutting for my enemies, whom He prunes and cuts down.

15:2.headline: 'This is my God': they could point
15:2.body: The people say 'this is my God', as if pointing at Him. Rashi, from the Mekhilta, says God showed Himself so clearly that a maidservant at the sea saw what prophets never saw.

sources.quote: בכבודו נגלה עליהם והיו מראין אותו באצבע
sources.says: Rashi says God appeared to them in His glory and they pointed to Him with a finger.

sources.quote: ראתה שפחה על הים מה שלא ראו נביאים
sources.says: Rashi says a maidservant at the sea saw what the prophets did not see.

15:2.headline: Build Him a home, or tell His beauty?
15:2.body: Onkelos reads ואנוהו from נוה, a dwelling: 'I will build Him a Temple'. Rashi also gives נוי, beauty: 'I will tell the world of His beauty and praise'.

sources.quote: ואבני לה מקדשא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: and I will build Him a Temple.

sources.quote: ואנוהו לשון נוי, אספר נויו ושבחו לבאי עולם
sources.says: Rashi says ואנוהו is from beauty: I will tell His beauty and praise to all the world.

15:3.headline: God, 'a man of war'?
15:3.body: Calling God a man sounds bodily. Rashi says איש here means master, as Naomi's husband is 'her man', so God is master of wars, and Onkelos says 'Lord of victories in battle'.

sources.quote: בעל מלחמות, כמו "איש נעמי
sources.says: Rashi says it means master of wars, as in 'Naomi's man', her husband.

sources.quote: יי מרי נצחן קרביא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: the LORD is master of victories in battle.

15:4.headline: Sunk in mud, for the bricks and mortar
15:4.body: Rashi says טבע means sinking into mud. The sea turned to mud, to repay Egypt measure for measure for enslaving Israel with mortar and bricks.

sources.quote: אין טביעה אלא במקום טיט
sources.says: Rashi says sinking only happens in a place of mud.

sources.quote: שנעשה הים טיט, לגמל להם כמדתם ששעבדו את ישראל בחמר ובלבנים
sources.says: Rashi says the sea became mud, to pay them back for enslaving Israel with mortar and bricks.

15:5.headline: Like straw, like stone, like lead
15:5.body: The song says the Egyptians went down 'like stone', sank 'like lead', and were eaten 'like straw'. Rashi says each fits a different group: the wicked were tossed like straw, the middling sank like stone, and the better ones sank at once like lead.

sources.quote: הרשעים כקש, הולכים ומטרפין עולין ויורדין, בינונים כאבן, והכשרים כעופרת שנחו מיד
sources.says: Rashi says the wicked were like straw, tossed up and down; the middling like stone; the decent like lead, which came to rest at once.

15:8.headline: The waters piled up, or grew cunning?
15:8.body: Rashi reads נערמו from ערמה, a heap: the waters piled up like heaps of wheat. Onkelos reads it from ערמה, cunning: the waters 'grew wise', and Chizkuni says they grew wise to sweep away Egypt.

sources.quote: אנקלוס תרגם לשון ערמימות, ולשון צחות המקרא כמו "ערמת חטים
sources.says: Rashi says Onkelos translates it as cunning, but the plain sense is like 'a heap of wheat'.

sources.quote: חכימו מיא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: the waters grew wise.

sources.quote: חכמו לנער מצרים
sources.says: Chizkuni explains: they grew wise to shake off the Egyptians.

15:9.headline: Empty the sheath, or arm myself?
15:9.body: Rashi reads אריק as 'empty': drawing a sword empties its sheath. Bekhor Shor reads it as 'arm myself', like Abraham arming his men, וירק את חניכיו.

sources.quote: ועל שם שהוא מריק את התער בשליפתו ונשאר ריק, נופל בו לשון הרקה
sources.says: Rashi says it is called emptying because drawing the sword leaves the sheath empty.

sources.quote: איזיין בחרבי כמו (בראשית י״ד:י״ד) וירק את חניכיו
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says it means I will arm myself with my sword, like 'he armed his trained men'.

15:10.headline: You blew, or You came at dusk?
15:10.body: Rashi reads נשפת as 'You blew'. Ibn Ezra hears נשף, twilight: at dusk You brought the wind that drowned them.

sources.quote: נשפת. לשון הפחה
sources.says: Rashi says נשפת means blowing.

sources.quote: מגזרת נשף כי בנשף הבאת רוח שהטביע אותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from נשף, twilight: at dusk You brought a wind that drowned them.

15:11.headline: Who is like You among the mighty, or among the silent?
15:11.body: Rashi reads באלם as 'among the mighty', and Ramban as 'among the angels'. Since it is written without a yod, Chizkuni reads it as אלמים, the mute: who is like You, who stays silent when provoked?

sources.quote: באלם. בחזקים
sources.says: Rashi says it means among the mighty.

sources.quote: אבל מי כמכה באלים במלאכי מעלה שהם נקראים אלים
sources.says: Ramban says it means among the angels on high, who are called אלים.

sources.quote: כלומר מי כמוך באלמים ובשתקנים שאין שתקן כמוך שמכעיסים אותך ואתה שותק
sources.says: Chizkuni says: who is like You among the mute and silent, for none is as silent as You, who are angered and stay silent.

15:11.headline: Too awesome to praise
15:11.body: 'Awesome in praises': Rashi says people are afraid to praise God, lest their praise fall short. As the psalm says, for You silence is praise.

sources.quote: יראוי מלהגיד תהלותיך פן ימעטו
sources.says: Rashi says one is afraid to tell Your praises, lest they fall short.

sources.quote: כמו שכתוב "לך דומיה תהלה
sources.says: Rashi cites the verse: for You, silence is praise.

15:12.headline: Why the Egyptians earned a burial
15:12.body: The earth swallowed the drowned Egyptians, so they were buried. Rashi, from the Mekhilta, says they earned this because they had once said 'the LORD is the righteous one'.

sources.quote: מכאן שזכו לקבורה בשכר שאמרו ה' הצדיק
sources.says: Rashi says from here we learn they merited burial as a reward for saying 'the LORD is righteous'.

15:16.headline: The people God 'bought': cherished, or acquired as servants?
15:16.body: Rashi says 'whom You acquired' means 'whom You cherished', like something bought at a high price. Ibn Ezra says they had been Egypt's slaves, and God acquired them to be His servants.

sources.quote: חבבת משאר אמות, כחפץ הקנוי בדמים יקרים
sources.says: Rashi says You held them dear above other nations, like an object bought at a high price.

sources.quote: שהיו עבדים למצרים, ואתה קנית אותם להיותם לך לעבדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they were slaves to Egypt, and You acquired them to be Your servants.

15:17.headline: 'Bring them', not 'bring us'
15:17.body: Moses sings 'You will bring them in', not 'bring us'. Rashi says Moses was prophesying that he himself would not enter the land.

sources.quote: נתנבא משה שלא יכנס לארץ לכך לא נאמר "תביאנו
sources.says: Rashi says Moses prophesied that he would not enter the land, so it does not say 'bring us'.

15:17.headline: The world was made with one hand, the Temple with two
15:17.body: 'Your hands established it.' Rashi says the world was made with one hand, as Isaiah says, but the Temple with two, which shows how dear it is.

sources.quote: חביב בית המקדש, שהעולם נברא ביד אחת
sources.says: Rashi says the Temple is beloved, for the world was created with one hand.

sources.quote: ומקדש בשתי ידים
sources.says: Rashi says the Temple is made with two hands.

15:20.headline: Miriam 'the prophetess': what did she foresee?
15:20.body: Rashi says that when she was only Aaron's sister, before Moses was born, she foretold that her mother would bear a son. Rashbam says נביאה here means one who speaks words of praise, as she does in her song.

sources.quote: היכן נתנבאה? כשהיתה אחות אהרן, קדם שנולד משה, אמרה עתידה אמי שתלד בן
sources.says: Rashi asks where she prophesied, and answers: as Aaron's sister, before Moses was born, she said her mother would bear a son.

sources.quote: הנביאה - קורא בעל דברי שבח
sources.says: Rashbam says a נביאה is one who speaks words of praise.

15:20.headline: Why 'Aaron's sister' and not Moses'?
15:20.body: Rashi says Aaron gave himself for her when she was struck with leprosy, so she is named for him. Ramban says it honors Aaron, who is not named in the song.

sources.quote: לפי שמסר נפשו עליה כשנצטרעה נקראת על שמו
sources.says: Rashi says because Aaron gave himself for her when she became leprous, she is called by his name.

sources.quote: מפני שהזכרו בשירה משה ומרים ולא הזכר אהרן רצה הכתוב להזכירו
sources.says: Ramban says Moses and Miriam are named in the song and Aaron is not, so the verse wanted to mention him.

15:20.headline: Drums in the desert
15:20.body: Where did the women get drums? Rashi says the righteous women were so sure God would do miracles that they brought drums out of Egypt.

sources.quote: מבטחות היו צדקניות שבדור שהקב"ה עושה להם נסים והוציאו תפים ממצרים
sources.says: Rashi says the righteous women of the generation were sure God would do miracles for them, and took drums out of Egypt.

15:22.headline: Moses had to pull them away from the sea
15:22.body: ויסע means Moses made them travel, not just that they traveled. Rashi says he had to move them against their will, since they were busy gathering the gold and jewels from the Egyptians' horses washed up by the sea.

sources.quote: ויסע - הפעיל
sources.says: Rashbam says ויסע is causative: he made them travel.

sources.quote: הסיען בעל כרחם, שעטרו מצרים את סוסיהם בתכשיטי זהב וכסף ואבנים טובות
sources.says: Rashi says he moved them against their will, because the Egyptians had decked their horses with gold, silver and jewels.

15:25.headline: God did not just show Moses a tree, He taught him
15:25.body: We expect 'showed him' a tree, but ויורהו means 'taught him', and Onkelos also says 'taught'. Ramban cites a midrash: God taught Moses His way, which is to sweeten the bitter with the bitter.

sources.quote: ואלפה יי אעא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: and the LORD taught him a tree.

sources.quote: ובעבור שלא מצאתי לשון מורה אלא בענין למוד
sources.says: Ramban says he has found this verb only in the sense of teaching.

sources.quote: שהורהו ולמדהו דרכו של הקב"ה שהוא ממתיק המר במר
sources.says: Ramban cites the midrash: God taught him His way, that He sweetens the bitter with the bitter.

15:25.headline: Laws given at Marah, before Sinai
15:25.body: What law was given at Marah, before the Torah at Sinai? Rashi, from the Talmud, says a few sections to study: Shabbat, the red heifer, and civil law.

sources.quote: במרה נתן להם מקצת פרשיות של תורה שיתעסקו בהם, שבת ופרה אדמה ודינין
sources.says: Rashi says at Marah God gave them a few sections of the Torah to study: Shabbat, the red heifer, and laws.

15:26.headline: God the healer: curing sickness, or preventing it?
15:26.body: Rashi's plain reading: God is like a doctor who says 'do not eat this' so you never get sick. Rashbam ties it to the story: the God who just healed the bitter water.

sources.quote: כרופא הזה האומר לאדם, אל תאכל דבר זה פן יביאך לידי חלי זה
sources.says: Rashi says it is like a doctor who tells a person: do not eat this, lest it bring you to this illness.

sources.quote: לא אשים עליך כי אני ה' רפאך - אשר רפאתי למים
sources.says: Rashbam says 'I am the LORD your healer' means the One who healed the water.

16:4.headline: What was the manna testing?
16:4.body: Rashi says the test was keeping the manna's rules: leave none overnight and do not gather on Shabbat. Ramban says the test was living with no food in hand, and Maimonides says it showed the world that God feeds those who serve him.

sources.quote: אם ישמרו מצוות התלויות בו, שלא יותירו ממנו ולא יצאו בשבת ללקט
sources.says: Rashi says the test is whether they keep the commands tied to the manna: leave none over, and do not go out to gather on Shabbat.

sources.quote: כי נסיון הוא להם שלא היה בידם מזון
sources.says: Ramban says the test was that they had no food in their hands.

sources.quote: שמי שמתמסר לעבודתו יתעלה, ה' יפרנס אותו ממקור שאינו עולה על הדעת
sources.says: Maimonides says it was so the world would learn that God provides for those devoted to him, from a source no one expects.

16:7.headline: Not just complaining, but getting everyone else to complain
16:7.body: The verb could mean 'you complain' or 'you make others complain'. Rashi says the doubled letter and the way the word is read force the second: they were turning their families and everyone else against Moses and Aaron.

sources.quote: שתרעימו עלינו את הכל, ואת בניכם ונשיכם ובנותיכם וערב רב
sources.says: Rashi says they were stirring up everyone against Moses and Aaron: their sons, wives, daughters and the mixed crowd.

sources.quote: ועל כרחי אני זקוק לפרש תלינו בלשון תפעילו מפני דגשותו וקריתו
sources.says: Rashi says the dagesh and the way the word is read force him to read it as causing others to complain.

16:13.headline: A layer of dew, or dew coming down?
16:13.body: Rashi reads it as a layer of dew lying over the manna, with dew under it too, so it was kept as if in a box. Ibn Ezra reads it as the dew coming down.

sources.quote: הטל שוכב על המן
sources.says: Rashi says the dew lay on top of the manna.

sources.quote: הרי הוא כמנח בקפסא
sources.says: Rashi says the manna was kept like something placed in a box.

sources.quote: ונבלי שמים מי ישכיב (איוב לח לז) טעם ירידה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares the verb in Job and says it means coming down.

16:14.headline: A word found nowhere else: what did the manna look like?
16:14.body: This word appears only here, so the commentators guess from related words. Rashi says uncovered, Onkelos says peeled, Ibn Ezra says round, and Rashbam says scattered.

sources.quote: מגלה, ואין דומה לו במקרא
sources.says: Rashi says it means uncovered, and that it has no match in Scripture.

sources.quote: דעדק מקלף
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as peeled.

sources.quote: כמו עגול ואין לו חבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means something like round, and the word has no partner.

sources.quote: אין לו חבר ופתרונו [לפי] עניינו מפוזר
sources.says: Rashbam says it has no partner, and from context it means scattered.

16:15.headline: The food was named after a question: what is it?
16:15.body: The Mekhilta and Rashbam hear the question 'what is it?' in the name, and Rashbam says מן meant 'what' in the language of Egypt. Rashi reads it instead as food made ready.

sources.quote: כאדם שאומר לחברו 'מה הוא?' כך אמרו זה לזה 'מה הוא?'
sources.says: The Mekhilta says they asked each other 'what is it?', the way a person asks a friend.

sources.quote: ולפי שהוא לשון מצרי ובאותו לשון היו רגילין שהוא כמו מה
sources.says: Rashbam says מן is an Egyptian word meaning 'what', the language they were used to.

sources.quote: הכנת מזון הוא, כמו "וימן להם המלך"
sources.says: Rashi says מן means food prepared, like 'the king assigned them' in Daniel.

16:20.headline: The manna bred worms, then stank: a story told backwards?
16:20.body: וירם comes from רמה, a worm, and since food usually smells before it breeds worms, Rashi says the verse tells it out of order. Ramban says this rot was a miracle, so the worms may really have come first.

sources.quote: וירם תולעים. לשון רמה
sources.says: Rashi says וירם comes from רמה, worm.

sources.quote: הרי זה מקרא הפוך, שבתחלה הבאיש ולבסוף התליע
sources.says: Rashi says the verse is reversed: first it stank, then it bred worms.

sources.quote: אבל זה שהתליע בדרך נס יתכן שהרים תולעים תחלה
sources.says: Ramban says that since this happened by miracle, the worms may have come first.

16:22.headline: Double bread, and bread that had changed
16:22.body: לחם משנה means a double portion of bread. A midrash quoted by Rashi also hears 'changed' in משנה: on Friday the manna changed for the better in smell and taste.

sources.quote: משנה, אותו היום נשתנה לשבח בריחו וטעמו
sources.says: Rashi quotes a midrash: on that day it changed for the better in smell and taste.

16:24.headline: Only twice in the Bible: no worms on Shabbat
16:24.body: Rabbeinu Bahya notes that ורמה, 'and worms', appears only twice in the Bible: in Job worms cover the dead, and here no worm touched the manna kept for Shabbat. He reads this as a hint that the dead rest on Shabbat.

sources.quote: ואין בכל המקרא ורמה כי אם שנים
sources.says: Bahya says the form ורמה appears only twice in Scripture.

sources.quote: מכאן רמז וסמך שהמתים יש להם מנוחה בשבת
sources.says: Bahya says this is a hint that the dead have rest on Shabbat.

16:25.headline: Three times 'today': the source of three Shabbat meals
16:25.body: Moses says 'today' three times in one verse. The Talmud learns from this that a person eats three meals on Shabbat, and Rabbeinu Bahya repeats it.

sources.quote: כמה סעודות חייב אדם לאכול בשבת — שלש
sources.says: The Talmud asks how many meals one must eat on Shabbat and answers three, from this verse.

sources.quote: ונזכרת מלת היום ג' פעמים בכתוב לרמוז על שלש סעודות בשבת
sources.says: Bahya says 'today' is said three times to hint at three Shabbat meals.

16:29.headline: 'Do not leave your place' and the Shabbat walking limit
16:29.body: The sages tied the limit on how far one may walk outside town on Shabbat, 2,000 cubits, to the words 'let no one leave his place'. Rashi adds that this limit is a rule of the sages, and the verse itself was said about people going out to gather manna.

sources.quote: אלו אלפים אמה של תחום שבת
sources.says: Rashi says this refers to the 2,000-cubit Shabbat limit.

sources.quote: ועקרו של מקרא על לוקטי המן נאמר
sources.says: Rashi says the plain point of the verse is about those gathering manna.

16:32.headline: Jeremiah shows the jar of manna to his generation
16:32.body: Rashi says that when people in Jeremiah's time said they could not study Torah because they had to earn a living, Jeremiah brought out the jar of manna. He told them: this is how God fed your ancestors.

sources.quote: הוציא להם צנצנת המן
sources.says: Rashi says Jeremiah brought out the jar of manna.

sources.quote: בזה נתפרנסו אבותיכם
sources.says: Rashi says Jeremiah told them: with this your ancestors were fed.

17:5.headline: Pass on ahead of the people, and see if they stone you
17:5.body: Ramban notes that עבר can mean to move away from someone, or to go on ahead of them. Rashi reads it as a rebuke to Moses, who had just said 'they will soon stone me': walk out in front of them and see if they do. Why did you speak badly of my children?

sources.quote: שֶׁתַּעֲבֹר מֵהֶם אֶל אַחֵר
sources.says: Ramban gives one sense: that you pass from them to another place.

sources.quote: שֶׁקָּדַם לָלֶכֶת קֹדֶם לָהֶם
sources.says: Ramban gives a second sense: to go on ahead of them.

sources.quote: וּרְאֵה אִם יִסְקְלוּךָ, לָמָּה הוֹצֵאתָ לַעַז עַל בָּנַי
sources.says: Rashi has God say: see if they stone you; why did you speak ill of my children?

17:5.headline: The staff that struck the Nile now brings water
17:5.body: Why mention that this staff struck the Nile? Rashi says the people thought the staff brought only disaster. Now they would see it could bring good too. Ramban adds that it once turned water to blood, and now it draws water from a rock.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים עַל הַמַּטֶּה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּכָן אֶלָּא לְפֻרְעָנוּת
sources.says: Rashi says Israel claimed the staff was only for bringing punishment.

sources.quote: יִרְאוּ עַתָּה שֶׁאַף לְטוֹבָה הוּא מוּכָן
sources.says: Rashi says now they would see it was ready for good as well.

sources.quote: כִּי אָז הָפַךְ הַמַּיִם לְדָם וְהֵסִיר אוֹתָם מִטִּבְעָם, וְעַתָּה יָבִיא מַיִם בְּצוּר הַחַלָּמִישׁ
sources.says: Ramban says the staff once turned water into blood, and now it will bring water out of flint.

17:6.headline: Strike 'into' the rock, not 'on' it
17:6.body: The verse says בצור, into the rock, not על הצור, on the rock. Rashi learns that the staff was made of a very hard stone called sanpirinon, and the rock split open in front of it.

sources.quote: עַל הַצּוּר לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא בַצּוּר, מִכָּאן שֶׁהַמַּטֶּה הָיָה שֶׁל מִין דָּבָר חָזָק וּשְׁמוֹ סַנְפִּירִינוֹן, וְהַצּוּר נִבְקַע מִפָּנָיו
sources.says: Rashi says the verse says 'into the rock', not 'on the rock', so the staff was of a hard stone called sanpirinon and the rock split before it.

17:7.headline: Massah and Meribah: one place, two complaints
17:7.body: The verse explains both names: מריבה, quarrel, because they quarreled with Moses, and מסה, testing, because they tested God. Ibn Ezra says there were two groups. One had no water and quarreled with Moses. The other still had water and wanted to test God.

sources.quote: ושב לפרש קריאת מריבה על ריב בני ישראל עם משה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the verse goes back to explain the name Meribah by Israel's quarrel with Moses, and Massah by their testing God.

sources.quote: כי שתים כתות היו, האחד אין להם מים לשתות, והיא העושה מריבה עם משה, והשנית יש להם מים שהביאו מאלוש, והיא הרוצה לנסות את השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says there were two groups: one without water that quarreled with Moses, and one with water from Alush that wanted to test God.

17:9.headline: 'Choose for us': Moses puts his student beside himself
17:9.body: Moses says 'choose for us', not 'for me'. Rashi says he made Joshua his equal. From this the sages taught: let your student's honor be as dear to you as your own.

sources.quote: לִי וּלְךָ – הִשְׁוָהוּ לוֹ; מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים יְהִי כְבוֹד תַּלְמִידְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלָּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says 'for us' means for me and you, putting Joshua level with himself, and the sages learned that a student's honor should be as dear as one's own.

17:11.headline: Did Moses' raised hands win the battle?
17:11.body: The Mishnah asks this and answers no. When Israel looked upward and gave their hearts to their Father in heaven, they prevailed; when not, they fell. Rashbam gives a plain reading: soldiers fight on while they see the banner held high.

sources.quote: וְכִי יָדָיו שֶׁל משֶׁה עוֹשׂוֹת מִלְחָמָה אוֹ שׁוֹבְרוֹת מִלְחָמָה. אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לְךָ, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִסְתַּכְּלִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה וּמְשַׁעְבְּדִין אֶת לִבָּם לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם הָיוּ מִתְגַּבְּרִים
sources.says: The Mishnah asks whether Moses' hands made or broke the war, and says Israel prevailed whenever they looked upward and gave their hearts to God.

sources.quote: שכן דרך עורכי מלחמה, כל זמן שרואים הרמת נסים
sources.says: Rashbam says that soldiers fight harder as long as they see the banners raised.

17:12.headline: Why Moses' hands grew heavy
17:12.body: Rashi says Moses' hands grew heavy because he was slow to do the task himself and sent someone else in his place. Ibn Ezra reads it plainly: no one can hold up his hands for a whole day.

sources.quote: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁנִּתְעַצֵּל בַּמִּצְוָה וּמִנָּה אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו, נִתְיַקְּרוּ יָדָיו
sources.says: Rashi says his hands grew heavy because he was lax in the commandment and appointed another in his place.

sources.quote: ידענו כי אין כח באדם להרים ידיו יום שלם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says no person has the strength to hold his hands up for a whole day.

17:12.headline: A stone, not a cushion
17:12.body: They set a stone under Moses. Rashi says he refused a pillow: while Israel was suffering, he wanted to suffer with them.

sources.quote: וְלֹא יָשַׁב לוֹ עַל כַּר וָכֶסֶת. אָמַר: יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין בְּצַעַר, אַף אֲנִי אֶהְיֶה עִמָּהֶם בְּצַעַר
sources.says: Rashi says Moses did not sit on a cushion, saying: Israel is in distress, so I will be in distress with them.

17:12.headline: Until sunset: Moses spoiled Amalek's star-charts
17:12.body: Rashi says the Amalekites used astrology to pick the hours when they would win. Moses held the sun in place and threw their hour-count into confusion.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ עֲמָלֵקִים מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶת הַשָּׁעוֹת בָּאִיצְטְרוּלוֹגִיאָה, בְּאֵיזוֹ שָׁעָה הֵם נוֹצְחִים, וְהֶעֱמִיד לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה חַמָּה וְעִרְבֵּב אֶת הַשָּׁעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the Amalekites figured out by astrology which hours they would win in, and Moses stopped the sun and mixed up the hours.

17:13.headline: Joshua 'weakened' Amalek: killed them, or left only the weak
17:13.body: ויחלש is a rare verb. Rashi reads it from חלש, weak: Joshua cut down their mighty men and left only the weak. Rashbam says it simply means he beat them. Bekhor Shor points to Job, where the same verb means dying.

sources.quote: חָתַךְ רָאשֵׁי גִבּוֹרָיו וְלֹא הִשְׁאִיר אֶלָּא חַלָּשִׁים שֶׁבָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says Joshua cut down the heads of their warriors and left only their weak ones.

sources.quote: ויחלש - נצחם. כדכתיב: קול ענות חלושה
sources.says: Rashbam says ויחלש means he defeated them, as in 'the sound of the cry of defeat'.

sources.quote: וגבר ימות ויחלש אלמא חלשות שייך בלשון מיתה
sources.says: Bekhor Shor cites Job, 'a man dies and is weakened', to show the word can mean death.

17:16.headline: A cut-short throne and a cut-short name
17:16.body: The verse says כס, not the full כסא, throne, and יה, not God's full name. Rashi says both are cut short on purpose. God swore that neither his name nor his throne is whole until Amalek's name is wiped out.

sources.quote: וּמַהוּ כֵּס וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר כִּסֵּא? וְאַף הַשֵּׁם נֶחֱלַק לְחֶצְיוֹ
sources.says: Rashi asks why it says כס and not כסא, and why even God's name is cut in half.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵין שְׁמוֹ שָׁלֵם וְאֵין כִּסְאוֹ שָׁלֵם עַד שֶׁיִּמָּחֶה שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק כֻּלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God swore that his name and his throne are not whole until Amalek's name is wholly erased.

17:16.headline: A hand raised in an oath, or a hand of power
17:16.body: Rashi reads 'a hand on the throne' as God's hand raised to swear. Chizkuni reads יד as power: once Israel has the strength to set a king on God's throne, the war on Amalek begins.

sources.quote: יָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּבָּ"ה הוּרְמָה לִשָּׁבַע בְּכִסְאוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God's hand was raised to swear by his throne.

sources.quote: יד לשון כח וממשלה
sources.says: Chizkuni says יד here means strength and rule.

sources.quote: כשיהיה כח ביד ישראל להעמיד להם מלך
sources.says: Chizkuni says it means when Israel has the power to set up a king for themselves.

18:1.headline: Seven names, and an extra letter for joining the people
18:1.body: Rashi lists seven names for Moses' father-in-law. He was called יתר because he added a section to the Torah, his advice on judges. When he joined Israel, one letter was added and he became יתרו.

sources.quote: שֶׁבַע שֵׁמוֹת נִקְרְאוּ לוֹ: רְעוּאֵל, יֶתֶר, יִתְרוֹ, חוֹבָב, חֶבֶר, קֵינִי, פּוּטִיאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says he had seven names: Reuel, Yeter, Yitro, Chovav, Chever, Keini, Putiel.

sources.quote: יֶתֶר, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁיִּתֵּר פָּרָשָׁה אַחַת בַּתּוֹרָה "וְאַתָּה תֶחֱזֶה"; יִתְרוֹ, לִכְשֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּר וְקִיֵּם הַמִּצְווֹת, הוֹסִיפוֹ לוֹ אוֹת אֶחָד עַל שְׁמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Yeter means he added a section to the Torah, and when he converted and kept the commandments a letter was added to his name.

18:7.headline: Who bowed to whom? The verse does not say
18:7.body: The verse says "he bowed and kissed him" without naming who. Rashi says the next words, "each man to his fellow", point to Moses, who is called "the man". Ibn Ezra agrees that the one who went out, Moses, bowed.

sources.quote: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לְמִי, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ, מִי הַקָּרוּי "אִישׁ" – מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know who bowed to whom, but "man" points to Moses, who is called "the man Moses".

sources.quote: ולפי הסברה כי היוצא הוא המשתחוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it makes sense that the one who went out is the one who bowed.

18:9.headline: Yitro rejoiced, or his skin crawled for Egypt
18:9.body: ויחד plainly means he rejoiced. Rashi brings the sages' play on חד, sharp: his skin prickled, grieving for Egypt. Rabbeinu Bahya adds a play on אחד, one: he declared God is one.

sources.quote: וַיִּשְׂמַח יִתְרוֹ, זֶהוּ פְּשׁוּטוֹ. וּמִ"אַ נַעֲשָׂה בְשָׂרוֹ חִדּוּדִין חִדּוּדִין, מֵצֵר עַל אִבּוּד מִצְרַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is that Yitro rejoiced, and a midrash says his flesh became prickly, pained over the loss of Egypt.

sources.quote: ועוד יש לומר ויחד מלשון אחדות לפי שנתגייר וייחד את הש"י וברך אותו
sources.says: Bahya says ויחד may also come from oneness: he converted, declared God one, and blessed him.

18:11.headline: The Egyptians were cooked in their own pot
18:11.body: זדו means they acted with malice. The sages hear in it the word for cooking stew, as in Jacob's stew. So the plan Egypt "cooked up", drowning the boys, came back on them at the sea.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר הִרְשִׁיעוּ. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ לְשׁוֹן וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד, בַּקְּדֵרָה אֲשֶׁר בִּשְּׁלוּ בָּהּ נִתְבַּשְּׁלוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means they acted wickedly, and the sages read it like "Jacob cooked a stew": they were cooked in the pot they cooked in.

sources.quote: בַּמַּיִם דִּמּוּ לְאַבְּדָם וְהֵם נֶאֶבְדוּ בַּמַּיִם
sources.says: Rashi says they planned to destroy Israel by water, and they were destroyed by water.

18:21.headline: "Choose" would do, but the verse says "see", as a prophet sees
18:21.body: Yitro tells Moses to pick judges, but uses תחזה, a word of vision. Rashi says Moses would choose by the holy spirit. Rabbeinu Bahya says the verse could have said "choose", and uses a prophet's word because only God sees the heart.

sources.quote: בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁעָלֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says Moses would see them through the holy spirit resting on him.

sources.quote: היה ראוי לומר ואתה תבחר כמו שאמר במעשה ויבחר משה אנשי חיל, אבל לפי שהאדם יראה לעינים וה' יראה ללבב על כן הוצרך לומר לשון תחזה שהוא לשון נבואה מלשון מחזה וחזון
sources.says: Bahya says the verse should have said "choose", but used תחזה, a word of prophecy, because a man sees the eyes and God sees the heart.

19:1.headline: "This day", not "that day": the Torah should feel new
19:1.body: The verse says they reached Sinai "on this day", where "on that day" would be expected. Rashi says the wording teaches that the Torah should feel new to you, as if it were given today.

sources.quote: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לִכְתֹּב אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא, מַהוּ בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה? שֶׁיִּהְיוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חֲדָשִׁים עָלֶיךָ כְּאִלּוּ הַיּוֹם נְתָנָם
sources.says: Rashi says the text could have said "that day"; it says "this day" so the Torah's words feel new, as if given today.

19:2.headline: "He camped": a whole people written as one person
19:2.body: The verse first says ויחנו, they camped, then ויחן, he camped. Rashi says Israel camped as one person with one heart, while Ibn Ezra says only the few tribal heads and elders camped facing the mountain.

sources.quote: כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בְּלֵב אֶחָד, אֲבָל שְׁאָר כָּל הַחֲנִיּוֹת בְּתַרְעוֹמוֹת וּבְמַחֲלֹקֶת
sources.says: Rashi says they camped like one person with one heart, while all their other camps were full of complaints and quarrels.

sources.quote: ומה שהזכיר לשון ויחן ולא אמר ויחנו למדך הכתוב מעלתם של ישראל שחנו כלם בלב אחד לקבל התורה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the singular shows that they all camped with one heart to receive the Torah.

sources.quote: כי ראשי המטות והזקנים חנו נגד ההר בעבור כבודם, על כן הזכיר ויחן כי מועטים היו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the tribal heads and elders camped facing the mountain, and the singular is used because they were few.

19:3.headline: Moses "went up" to God: a climb, and a turn of mind
19:3.body: Maimonides says "went up" here also means turning the mind toward something lofty, though Moses did climb the mountain too. Ramban says he climbed only to the edge of the mountain, not into the cloud where God was.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10
sources.quote: ואילו דבריו "ומשה עלה אל האלהים" (שמות יט,ג) הם במשמעות השלישית (=הפנייה במחשבה אל דבר נשגב), יחד עם זאת שהוא גם עלה אל ראש ההר
sources.says: Maimonides says "Moses went up to God" means turning the mind to something lofty, while he also climbed to the top of the mountain.

sources.quote: כִּי עָלָה אֶל קְצֵה הָהָר לְהִזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו, וְלֹא בָּא אֶל הָעֲרָפֶל אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הָאֱלֹהִים
sources.says: Ramban says Moses went up to the edge of the mountain to present himself, and did not enter the thick cloud where God was.

19:4.headline: Why eagles' wings: a parent that takes the arrow itself
19:4.body: Rashi says other birds carry their young in their feet, but the eagle carries them on its wings, saying better the arrow hit me than my child. God did the same, putting the cloud between Israel and the arrows of Egypt.

sources.quote: שֶׁכָּל שְׁאָר הָעוֹפוֹת נוֹתְנִים אֶת בְּנֵיהֶם בֵּין רַגְלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says all other birds carry their young between their feet.

sources.quote: לְכָךְ נוֹתְנוֹ עַל כְּנָפָיו, אוֹמֵר מוּטָב יִכָּנֵס הַחֵץ בִּי וְלֹא בִּבְנִי
sources.says: Rashi says the eagle puts its young on its wings, saying better the arrow enter me than my child.

sources.quote: כי הנשר יגביה למעלה מכל עוף והכל מפחדים ממנו והוא לא יפחד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the eagle flies higher than any bird; all fear it and it fears none.

19:5.headline: A treasure the king keeps in his own hand
19:5.body: Rashi says סגלה is a prized treasure, like the jewels kings store away. Ramban offers a second reading: it may mean being bound close to God.

sources.quote: אוֹצָר חָבִיב, כְּמוֹ "וּסְגֻלַּת מְלָכִים"
sources.says: Rashi says it means a beloved treasure, as in "the treasure of kings".

sources.quote: כְּדָבָר נֶחְמָד לֹא יִמְסְרֶנּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּיַד אַחֵר
sources.says: Ramban says it is like a precious thing the king will not hand to anyone else.

sources.quote: אוֹ יִהְיֶה "סְגֻלָּה" דְּבֵקוּת
sources.says: Ramban says סגלה may instead mean clinging close.

sources.quote: המטמון המוצנע והסמוי מן העין יקרא סגולה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says a hidden treasure, kept out of sight, is called סגולה.

19:6.headline: A kingdom of priests, or a kingdom of nobles?
19:6.body: Rashi says כהנים here means princes, as when King David's sons are called כהנים. Onkelos reads "kings and priests", and Ramban reads "a kingdom that serves me".

sources.quote: שָׂרִים, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר "וּבְנֵי דָּוִד כֹּהֲנִים"
sources.says: Rashi says it means princes, as in "and David's sons were כהנים".

sources.quote: קֳדָמַי מַלְכִין כָּהֲנִין וְעַם קַדִישׁ
sources.says: Onkelos translates "kings, priests, and a holy people".

sources.quote: וְתִהְיוּ מַמְלֶכֶת מְשָׁרְתַי
sources.says: Ramban says it means you will be a kingdom of my servants.

19:13.headline: Shot with arrows, or thrown down?
19:13.body: ירה usually means to shoot, but Rashi reads יירה as "thrown down to the ground", as in Pharaoh's army "thrown into the sea". Ibn Ezra keeps the usual sense: anyone too far away to stone is shot with arrows.

sources.quote: יֻשְׁלַךְ לְמַטָּה לָאָרֶץ, כְּמוֹ "יָרָה בַיָּם"
sources.says: Rashi says it means he will be thrown down to the ground, as in "he threw into the sea".

sources.quote: רק יסקלוהו הרואים ממקום מעמדם מיד, ואם רחוק יורוהו בחצים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says those who see him stone him from where they stand, and if he is far they shoot him with arrows.

19:13.headline: Yovel: a ram's horn, perhaps from the ram that replaced Isaac
19:13.body: Rashi says יובל means a ram's horn, since in Arabia a ram is called yovla, and that it came from the ram offered in place of Isaac. Ramban objects that Isaac's ram was burned whole, horns and all.

sources.quote: הוּא שׁוֹפָר שֶׁל אַיִל, שֶׁכֵּן בַּעֲרַבְיָא קוֹרִין לְדִכְרָא יוּבְלָא, וְשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל אַיִל שֶׁל יִצְחָק הָיָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a ram's horn, because in Arabia they call a ram yovla, and it was the horn of Isaac's ram.

sources.quote: במשוך היובל. פי' כבש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יובל means a ram.

sources.quote: וְלֹא הֲבִינוֹתִי זֶה, כִּי אֵילוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק עוֹלָה הִקְרִיב אוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says he does not understand this, since Isaac's ram was offered as a burnt offering.

19:17.headline: "To meet God": like a groom going out to his bride
19:17.body: Moses brings the people out "to meet God". Rashi says God's presence also came out to meet them, like a groom going out to meet his bride.

sources.quote: מַגִּיד שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה יָצְאָה לִקְרָאתָם כְּחָתָן הַיּוֹצֵא לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says God's presence went out to meet them like a groom going out to meet the bride.

19:17.headline: At the foot of the mountain, or underneath it?
19:17.body: Rashi says the plain meaning of בתחתית is the foot of the mountain, as Onkelos translates. The midrash reads it as "underneath": God lifted the mountain and held it over them like a barrel.

sources.quote: לְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ בְּרַגְלֵי הָהָר; וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁנִּתְלַשׁ הָהָר מִמְּקוֹמוֹ וְנִכְפָּה עֲלֵיהֶם כְּגִיגִית
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is at the foot of the mountain, and the midrash says the mountain was torn up and held over them like a barrel.

sources.quote: וְאִתְעַתָּדוּ בְּשִׁפּוֹלֵי טוּרָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates "they stood at the lower slopes of the mountain".

19:18.headline: A lime kiln: a small picture for something far bigger
19:18.body: Rashi says the furnace here is a lime kiln, though the fire really reached the heart of heaven. The Torah uses a picture people know so the ear can take in what it is able to hear.

sources.quote: הכבשן. שֶׁל סִיד; יָכוֹל כְּכִבְשָׁן זֶה וְלֹא יוֹתֵר
sources.says: Rashi says it is a lime kiln, and asks: could it be only as big as a kiln and no more?

sources.quote: וּמַה תַּ"לֹ כִּבְשָׁן? לְשַׂבֵּר אֶת הָאֹזֶן מַה שֶּׁהִיא יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁמֹעַ
sources.says: Rashi says the word kiln is used to let the ear hear what it can take in.

19:20.headline: God "came down" on Sinai: not a move from place to place
19:20.body: Maimonides says that when the Torah says God came down, it means God made himself known there, and Onkelos translates "God was revealed". Rashi says God spread the heavens over the mountain like a sheet on a bed.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10
sources.quote: כינה את ירידת ההתגלות על הנביא או שריית השכינה במקום מסוים "ירידה"
sources.says: Maimonides says Scripture calls God's revelation to a prophet, or his presence resting in a place, a coming down.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10
sources.quote: ואילו המשמעות הראשונה, כלומר ההתגלות והכבוד, שכיחה: "וירדתי ודברתי עמך" (במדבר יא,יז), "וירד ה' על הר סיני"
sources.says: Maimonides gives "God came down on Mount Sinai" as an example of this meaning: revelation and glory.

sources.quote: וְאִתְגְלִי יְיָ עַל טוּרָא דְסִינַי
sources.says: Onkelos translates "and God was revealed on Mount Sinai".

sources.quote: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִרְכִּין שָׁמַיִם הָעֶלְיוֹנִים וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנִים וְהִצִּיעָן עַל גַּבֵּי הָהָר כְּמַצָּע עַל הַמִּטָּה
sources.says: Rashi says God bent down the upper and lower heavens and spread them on the mountain like a sheet on a bed.

19:22.headline: Priests before there were priests: who were they?
19:22.body: No priests had been appointed yet, so Rashi says these are the firstborn, who did the service then. Rabbeinu Bahya also suggests Aaron's sons, called priests for what they would become.

sources.quote: אַף הַבְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה בָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says even the firstborn, who performed the service.

sources.quote: או יש לפרש הכהנים על בני אהרן ממש ונקראו כהנים על שם העתיד
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says it could mean Aaron's actual sons, called priests for what they would later be.

sources.quote: ואין לומר כהנים ממש שהרי עדיין לא נתכהנו
sources.says: Chizkuni says they cannot be actual priests, since no one had yet been made a priest.

2:1.headline: Amram "took" a wife he had already married
2:1.body: The verse says Amram took a daughter of Levi as if for the first time. Rashi says he had separated from her because of Pharaoh's decree, then took her back in a second wedding, and she became young again.

sources.quote: פָּרוּשׁ הָיָה מִמֶּנָּה מִפְּנֵי גְּזֵרַת פַּרְעֹה, וְהֶחֱזִירָהּ וְעָשָׂה בָהּ לִקּוּחִין שְׁנִיִּים, וְאַף הִיא נֶהֶפְכָה לִהְיוֹת נַעֲרָה
sources.says: Rashi says Amram had separated from her because of Pharaoh's decree, then took her back with a second marriage, and she turned young again.

2:2.headline: "She saw he was good", like God seeing the light
2:2.body: The Talmud gives several readings of טוב. Some say it was his name, or that he was fit for prophecy. The sages say the house filled with light, since Genesis uses the same words: God saw the light, that it was good.

sources.quote: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: ״טוֹב״ שְׁמוֹ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״טוֹבִיָּה״ שְׁמוֹ. רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: הָגוּן לִנְבִיאוּת
sources.says: Rabbi Meir says his name was Tov, Rabbi Yehuda says Toviah, and Rabbi Nehemiah says he was fit for prophecy.

sources.quote: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה, נִתְמַלֵּא הַבַּיִת כּוּלּוֹ אוֹר. כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וַתֵּרֶא אוֹתוֹ כִּי טוֹב הוּא״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב״
sources.says: The sages say the house filled with light when Moses was born, comparing this verse to "God saw the light, that it was good".

2:3.headline: Pitch outside, clay inside, so the baby would not smell it
2:3.body: The basket was sealed with clay and pitch. Rashi says the pitch went outside so the righteous child would not smell its bad odor. Rashbam gives a practical reason: pitch outside keeps the water out.

sources.quote: זֶפֶת מִבַּחוּץ וְטִיט מִבִּפְנִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יָרִיחַ אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק רֵיחַ רַע שֶׁל זֶפֶת
sources.says: Rashi says pitch was outside and clay inside, so the righteous child would not smell the pitch.

sources.quote: ובזפת - מבחוץ שלא יכנסו בו המים
sources.says: Rashbam says the pitch was outside so water would not get in.

2:5.headline: The maids were "walking", that is, about to die
2:5.body: Her maids were "walking" by the river. Rabbi Yohanan reads "walking" as "going to die", as Esau said "I am going to die". Rashi explains: they protested when she wanted to save the child.

sources.quote: אֵין הֲלִיכָה זוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן מִיתָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ לָמוּת״
sources.says: Rabbi Yohanan says this walking means dying, as in "I am going to die".

sources.quote: הוֹלְכוֹת לָמוּת לְפִי שֶׁמִּחוּ בָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says they were going to die because they objected to her.

2:5.headline: She sent her maid, or stretched out her arm
2:5.body: אמתה can mean "her maidservant" or, read as אמה, "her forearm". The Talmud records both views. Rashi adds the midrash that her arm stretched many cubits to reach the basket.

sources.quote: חַד אָמַר: יָדָהּ, וְחַד אָמַר: שִׁפְחָתָהּ
sources.says: One sage says it means her hand, the other says her maidservant.

sources.quote: וְהֵם דָּרְשׁוּ אֶת אֲמָתָהּ – אֶת יָדָהּ, וְנִשְׁתַּרְבְּבָה אַמָּתָהּ אַמּוֹת הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says the rabbis read it as her hand, and her arm stretched out many cubits.

2:6.headline: "She saw him, the child": who else did she see?
2:6.body: The verse says "she saw him" and then names "the child", which seems doubled. Rashi gives the plain reading, then a midrash: she saw God's presence with him.

sources.quote: אֶת מִי רָאֲתָה? את הילד, זֶהוּ פְּשׁוּטוֹ. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ (שם), שֶׁרָאֲתָה עִמּוֹ שְׁכִינָה
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is that she saw the child, and the midrash says she saw the Shekhinah with him.

2:7.headline: Why a Hebrew nurse: the baby refused the others
2:7.body: Miriam offers a Hebrew nurse. Rashi says Pharaoh's daughter had already tried many Egyptian women, but the baby would not nurse, because his mouth would one day speak with God.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֶחֱזִירַתּוּ עַל מִצְרִיּוֹת הַרְבֵּה לִינֹק וְלֹא יָנַק, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה עָתִיד לְדַבֵּר עִם הַשְּׁכִינָה
sources.says: Rashi says she took him to many Egyptian women and he would not nurse, because he was destined to speak with the Shekhinah.

2:9.headline: "Take this child" also says "here, he is yours"
2:9.body: Pharaoh's daughter says היליכי, "take away", to Moses' own mother. The Talmud splits the word into הא שליכי, "here, it is yours". She prophesied without knowing it.

sources.quote: מִתְנַבְּאָה וְאֵינָהּ יוֹדַעַת מָה מִתְנַבְּאָה, ״הֵילִיכִי״ — הָא שֶׁלִּיכִי
sources.says: The Talmud says she prophesied without knowing it: היליכי means "here is what is yours".

2:10.headline: Not "drawn out" but "one who draws out"
2:10.body: The name משה is in the active form: "one who draws out", not "one drawn out". Chizkuni and Sforno say this points to his future: he will rescue others. Ibn Ezra thinks the name was translated from Egyptian.

sources.quote: משוי אין כתיב כאן אלא משה, לומר כשם שמשיתיהו כן יהיה הוא מושה אחרים
sources.says: Chizkuni notes it says Moshe, not Mashui, to teach that just as he was drawn out, he will draw out others.

sources.quote: מְמַלֵּט וּמוֹשֶׁה אֶת אֲחֵרִים מִצָּרָה
sources.says: Sforno says the name means one who rescues and draws others out of trouble.

sources.quote: שם משה מתורגם מלשון מצרים בלשון הקדש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the name Moshe is a Hebrew translation of an Egyptian name.

2:11.headline: Moses "grew" twice: in height, then in rank
2:11.body: Verse 10 already said the child grew. Rashi brings Rabbi Yehuda: the first time means he grew tall, the second that he grew great, when Pharaoh put him over his household.

sources.quote: הָרִאשׁוֹן לְקוֹמָה וְהַשֵּׁנִי לִגְדֻלָּה, שֶׁמִּנָּהוּ פַּרְעֹה עַל בֵּיתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the first "grew" is in height and the second in greatness, since Pharaoh appointed him over his house.

2:13.headline: "Why will you hit him?": wicked before the blow lands
2:13.body: Moses asks "why will you strike" in the future tense. Rashi says the man had not hit yet, but he is already called wicked for raising his hand.

sources.quote: אַעַ"פִּ שֶׁלֹּא הִכָּהוּ נִקְרָא רָשָׁע בַּהֲרָמַת יָד
sources.says: Rashi says that even though he had not hit him, he is called wicked for raising his hand.

2:14.headline: "Are you saying you will kill me?": killing with a word
2:14.body: The Hebrew says "do you say to kill me". The midrash Rashi cites takes "say" literally: Moses had killed the Egyptian by speaking God's name.

sources.quote: מִכָּאן אָנוּ לְמֵדִים שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ בַּשֵּׁם הַמְפֹרָשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says we learn from here that Moses killed him with the explicit name of God.

2:14.headline: "The thing is known": now Moses understands the slavery
2:14.body: Plainly, Moses fears his killing has become known. Rashi brings a midrash: now Moses understood what had puzzled him, why Israel deserved such hard slavery.

sources.quote: נוֹדַע לִי הַדָּבָר שֶׁהָיִיתִי תָּמֵהַּ עָלָיו, מֶה חָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכָּל שִׁבְעִים אֻמּוֹת לִהְיוֹת נִרְדִּים בַּעֲבוֹדַת פֶּרֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash: Moses now understood what he wondered about, how Israel sinned more than seventy nations to deserve hard labor.

2:15.headline: He stayed in Midian, and sat by a well like Jacob
2:15.body: The same word וישב appears twice. Rashi says the first means he settled in Midian. The second means he sat down by the well, having learned from Jacob, who found his wife at a well.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן יְשִׁיבָה. לָמַד מִיַּעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּזְדַּוֵּג לוֹ זִוּוּגוֹ מִן הַבְּאֵר
sources.says: Rashi says this one means sitting, and that Moses learned from Jacob, who met his match at a well.

sources.quote: נִתְעַכֵּב שָׁם; כְּמוֹ: "וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב"
sources.says: Rashi says the first וישב means he stayed there.

2:16.headline: Priest of Midian, or its chief who quit idol worship
2:16.body: Jethro is called כהן, which can mean priest or chief. Onkelos calls him "the great one of Midian". Rashi says he was their leader, but he left idol worship and they shunned him.

sources.quote: רַב שֶׁבָּהֶן; וּפָרַשׁ לוֹ מֵעֲ"זָ וְנִדּוּהוּ מֵאֶצְלָם
sources.says: Rashi says he was their chief, but he left idol worship and they banned him.

sources.quote: וּלְרַבָּא דְמִדְיָן שְׁבַע בְּנָן
sources.says: Onkelos translates: the great one of Midian had seven daughters.

2:20.headline: "Let him eat bread": perhaps he will marry one of you
2:20.body: Jethro tells his daughters to invite Moses to eat לחם, bread. Rashi reads it as a hint at marriage, since "bread" stands for Potiphar's wife in the Joseph story.

sources.quote: שֶׁמָּא יִשָּׂא אַחַת מִכֶּם; כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר: "כִּי אִם הַלֶּחֶם אֲשֶׁר הוּא אוֹכֵל"
sources.says: Rashi says: perhaps he will marry one of you, as in "except the bread that he eats" said of Potiphar's wife.

2:21.headline: Moses agreed to stay, or swore to stay
2:21.body: ויואל usually means "he agreed", and Onkelos reads it so. Rashi brings a midrash that hears אלה, "an oath": Moses swore not to leave Midian without Jethro's permission.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ: לְשׁוֹן אָלָה – נִשְׁבַּע לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יָזוּז מִמִּדְיָן כִּי אִם בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash that it means an oath: Moses swore not to leave Midian without Jethro's permission.

sources.quote: וּצְבִי משֶׁה לְמִיתַב עִם גַבְרָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: Moses was willing to live with the man.

2:23.headline: The king "died": really dead, or struck with leprosy?
2:23.body: Rashi brings a midrash that the king became a leper and bathed in the blood of Israelite babies. Ramban also gives the plain reading: the king really died, and the people groaned because the next king was even worse.

sources.quote: נִצְטָרַע וְהָיָה שׁוֹחֵט תִּינוֹקוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְרוֹחֵץ בְּדָמָם
sources.says: Rashi says the king became leprous and slaughtered Israelite children to bathe in their blood.

sources.quote: וְכַאֲשֶׁר רָאוּ שֶׁמֵּת הַמֶּלֶךְ הֵאָנְחוּ מְאֹד מִמְּלֹךְ אָדָם חָנֵף מַרְשִׁיעַ מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Ramban says that when they saw the king had died, they groaned because a worse, more wicked man now ruled.

20:2.headline: "I" (אנכי) read as "I Myself wrote and gave it"
20:2.body: The commandments open with אנכי, "I". A midrash quoted by Rabbeinu Bahya reads its letters as the first letters of an Aramaic sentence: אנא נפשאי כתבית יהבית, "I Myself wrote it and gave it".

sources.quote: ועוד אמרו במדרש כי יש במלת אנכ"י נוטריקון אנא נפשאי כתבית יהבית
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites a midrash that אנכי stands for "I Myself wrote it and gave it".

20:3.headline: "Before Me": in My presence, or as long as I exist?
20:3.body: Rashi reads על פני in time: no other gods as long as I exist, so the command holds for every generation. Ibn Ezra reads it as "in My presence", since God is present everywhere, and Maimonides lists "presence" as one meaning of פנים.

sources.quote: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֲנִי קַיָּם, שֶׁלֹּא תֹאמַר לֹא נִצְטַוּוּ עַל עֲ"זָ אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says it means as long as I exist, so no one can say only that generation was commanded.

sources.quote: והנה הטעם אחר שאני אלהיך ואני נמצא תמיד בכל מקום, ואני רואה מה תעשה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means: I am always present everywhere and see what you do.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 37
sources.quote: הוא גם שמם של נוכחות האדם ומקום הימצאו
sources.says: Maimonides says one meaning of פנים is a person's presence and the place where he is.

20:5.headline: A "jealous" God: a word kept for idol worship alone
20:5.body: Rashi reads קנא as zealous to punish, a God who does not let idol worship pass. Maimonides and Rabbeinu Bahya point out that the Bible speaks of God's jealousy only about idol worship.

sources.quote: מְקַנֵּא לִפָּרַע וְאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עַל מִדָּתוֹ לִמְחֹל עַל עֲבוֹדַת אֱלִילִים
sources.says: Rashi says God is zealous to punish and does not set aside His way to forgive idol worship.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 36
sources.quote: לא תמצא לשון חרון אף ולא לשון כעס ולא לשון קנאה אלא בעבודה זרה דווקא
sources.says: Maimonides says words of anger and jealousy are used of God only about idol worship.

sources.quote: ודע כי לא תמצא בכל התורה קנאה בהקב"ה כי אם בעון
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the Torah speaks of God's jealousy only for the sin of idol worship.

20:5.headline: "Those who hate Me": only children who keep the sin
20:5.body: The last word limits the punishment. Onkelos, Rashi, and Rashbam say the children suffer only if they too hate God and keep doing what their parents did.

sources.quote: לְשָׂנְאָי כַּד מְשַׁלְמִין בְּנַיָא לְמֶחֱטֵי בָּתַר אֲבָהָתְהוֹן
sources.says: Onkelos translates: to those who hate Me, when the children go on sinning after their fathers.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁאוֹחֲזִין מַעֲשֵׂה אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם בִּידֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means when they hold on to their fathers' deeds.

sources.quote: לשנאי - אם הבנים שונאי
sources.says: Rashbam says it means if the children hate Me.

20:7.headline: The same word twice: "falsely" and "for nothing"
20:7.body: שוא can mean "false" or "empty, pointless", and the verse uses it twice. Onkelos and Sforno both give the two uses different senses, so the verse forbids false oaths and also needless ones.

sources.quote: לְמַגָנָא אֲרֵי לָא יִזַכֵּי יְיָ יָת דִיֵימֵי בִשְׁמֵהּ לְשִׁקְרָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates the first לשוא as "for nothing" and the second as "falsely".

sources.quote: לַשָּׁוְא. לַשֶּׁקֶר
sources.says: Sforno says the first לשוא means falsely.

sources.quote: לְהֶבֶל וּבִלְתִּי צֹרֶךְ, כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיִּשָּׁבַע עַל הָאֱמֶת
sources.says: Sforno says the second means for no need, even when the oath is true.

20:8.headline: "Remember" here, "keep" in Deuteronomy: why two words?
